sections.title: Hands and standing
sections.transition: Great — now some quick questions about you and your world.

blocks.name: Edinburgh Handedness Inventory – Short Form
blocks.citation: Veale, J. F. (2014). Edinburgh Handedness Inventory – Short Form: A revised version based on confirmatory factor analysis. Laterality, 19(2), 164-177. (Original: Oldfield, 1971.)

licence.evidence: Permission held by the research team and filed in the study's licence register (D-10).

blocks.instructions: Please indicate your preferences in the use of hands in the following activities.

stem.text: Which hand do you write with?

items.hint: Think about what you'd do without stopping to think about it. If you really would use either hand, choose "Both equally".

stem.text: Which hand do you throw a ball with?

items.hint: Think about what you'd do without stopping to think about it. If you really would use either hand, choose "Both equally".

stem.text: Which hand do you hold your toothbrush in?

items.hint: Think about what you'd do without stopping to think about it. If you really would use either hand, choose "Both equally".

stem.text: Which hand do you hold a spoon in?

items.hint: Think about what you'd do without stopping to think about it. If you really would use either hand, choose "Both equally".

stem.text: Your answers suggest you're {band}

lede.text: Your handedness score is {lq}, on a scale from -100 (always the left hand) to +100 (always the right hand).

items.researcherNote: Participant-facing feedback on the EHI laterality quotient (D-33). Presentational only — computed from the answers just given, stored nowhere, and shown after all four items so it cannot influence any of them.

blocks.name: MacArthur Scale of Subjective Social Status – Adult Version
blocks.citation: Adler, N. E., Epel, E. S., Castellazzo, G., & Ickovics, J. R. (2000). Relationship of subjective and objective social status with psychological and physiological functioning: preliminary data in healthy white women. Health Psychology, 19(6), 586–592.

licence.holder: SPARQ / MacArthur Network toolkit, with attribution
licence.evidence: Openly available and free to use for non-commercial research and clinical purposes (SPARQ toolkit); confirmed by the research team 2026-10-14 (D-61).

stem.text: Where would you be on this ladder?

lede.text:
Think of this ladder as representing where people stand in society in the UK.

At the top are the people who are best off — those who have the most money, the most education, and the most respected jobs.

At the bottom are the people who are worst off — those who have the least money, the least education, and the least respected jobs, or no job.

Where would you place yourself on this ladder at this time in your life?

items.topLabel: The people who are best off
items.bottomLabel: The people who are worst off

stem.text: Where would you be on this ladder?

lede.text:
Think of this ladder as representing where people stand in their communities.

People define community in different ways. Please think about the community that is most meaningful to you.

At the top of the ladder are the people who have the highest standing in their community. At the bottom are the people who have the lowest standing.

Where would you place yourself on this ladder at this time in your life?

items.topLabel: The people with the highest standing
items.bottomLabel: The people with the lowest standing

blocks.name: Sleep Quality Scale
blocks.citation: Snyder, E., Cai, B., DeMuro, C., Morrison, M. F., & Ball, W. (2018). A new single-item sleep quality scale: Results of psychometric evaluation in patients with chronic primary insomnia and depression. Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 14(11), 1849-1857.

licence.evidence: Item and anchors published in full in Snyder et al. (2018). Terms of use for this study not yet confirmed with the authors (D-53).

stem.text: During the past 7 days, how would you rate your sleep quality overall?

lede.text: Think about how many hours you slept, how easily you fell asleep, how often you woke up in the night, whether you woke up earlier than you needed to, and how refreshed you felt when you got up.

items.researcherNote: Published item and 0-10 anchors (Snyder et al., 2018), shown as one row with the bands beneath (D-53). The lede is the study's plain-language list of the factors the SQS asks people to consider.

blocks.name: Karolinska Sleepiness Scale
blocks.citation: Åkerstedt, T., & Gillberg, M. (1990). Subjective and objective sleepiness in the active individual. International Journal of Neuroscience, 52(1-2), 29-37.

stem.text: How sleepy are you feeling right now?

options.label: Sleepy, but no effort to keep awake
Sleepy, some effort to keep awake
Very sleepy, great effort to keep awake, fighting sleep

blocks.instructions: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?

stem.text: Feeling nervous, anxious or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless

sections.title: Phones and social media
sections.transition: Now some questions about phones and social media.

stem.text: Do you have your own smartphone?
How many smartphones do you currently own?
What type of smartphone are you using? Participants tick all that apply.
Please tell us what
At what age did you get your first smartphone? Please answer in years.

options.label: I’m not sure / I can’t remember

stem.text: Do you currently use social media?

lede.text: We mean apps where you can see or share things other people have posted — even if you mostly just watch.

stem.text: Just to check — do you use any of these?

lede.text:
TikTok · Instagram · Snapchat · YouTube · WhatsApp · Discord · Reddit · X (Twitter) · Twitch · BeReal · Facebook · Pinterest

Watching or reading without posting still counts. Messaging apps you use to keep up with friends count too.

items.researcherNote: Confirmation step for a 'No' to sm_use (D-26). Recorded separately from sm_use — the original answer is never overwritten — and the social-media section shows if EITHER says yes. A 'No' here is taken at face value and no app questions follow.

stem.text: At what age did you start using social media? Please answer in years.

options.label: I’m not sure / I can’t remember

stem.text: How often do you use AI chatbots or assistants?

lede.text: For example ChatGPT, Snapchat's My AI, Gemini, Copilot or Character.AI.

items.researcherNote: Study-written (D-59). Same steps as the social-media frequency questions. 1 = never; the follow-ups are asked of 2-5.

stem.text: What do you use them for?

items.researcherNote: Asked unless ai_use_frequency = Never (D-59). 6 (feelings) and 7 (friend or company) are kept apart from 5 (advice) to identify use as a confidant or companion; neither is a risk flag by itself. 8 = something else, described in ai_use_purpose_other.

options.label: Looking things up or answering questions
Creative things, like stories, pictures or music
Just for fun or to pass the time
Talking about my feelings or when I'm upset
Chatting to it as a friend or for company

stem.text: What else do you use them for?

items.researcherNote: Free text, asked only when 'Something else' is chosen in ai_use_purpose (D-59).

stem.text: After using AI chatbots, how do you usually feel?

items.researcherNote: Asked unless ai_use_frequency = Never (D-59).

stem.text: Which of these apps do you have on your phone?

groups.label: I have these apps on my phone
I don't have these apps on my phone

stem.text: On a typical day, how much time do you usually spend on each of the following apps?

lede.text: You may refer to your phone's Screen Time or Digital Wellbeing summary.

items.researcherNote: Stored as app_minutes_<code>, total minutes per app (codes from scale.sm_platforms). Apps not in 'have' are not_presented_branching.

stem.text: Do you think you spend too much time on social media?
On the social media site you use the most, is your account public or private?

items.researcherNote: Legacy tag typo 'Acount_privacy' preserved as alias (A-31).

stem.text: On the social media platform you use most often, would you describe yourself as more of an active or passive user?

options.label: Mostly active: I often post, comment, message, or share content
Mostly passive: I mostly look, scroll, or watch without posting much

stem.text: Why do you use social media? Select all that apply.

options.label: Stay in touch with friends or family
Keep up with news or current events
Find information or learn new things
Share my own content or express myself
Keep up with trends or viral content

stem.text: On a typical night, how many times do you wake up and check social media?
How long after waking do you typically check social media?
On a typical weekday (Monday–Friday), how much time do you spend using social media?
On a typical weekend day, holiday, or other day off, how much time do you spend using social media?

items.researcherNote: Legacy tag contains a slash and trailing space (A-31).

stem.text: I lose track of how much time I spend on social media
Do you use any features designed to reduce your social media use and/or screentime (e.g., screentime limits, break reminders, sleep hours reminders)?
What effect do you think abstaining from social media would have on you?

items.researcherNote: D-01/A-1: administered stem erroneously duplicated app_reduce; intended wording restored as revision 1 of the corrected item. Legacy data flagged unreliable in the crosswalk.

stem.text: How long do you think you could go without social media?

lede.text: We mean platforms like TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, Snapchat, X (Twitter), Reddit, YouTube and Threads — not messaging apps such as WhatsApp.

items.researcherNote: Legacy field was free text with no numeric validation (docs/10 §4); numeric control is a PRESENT-disposition modernisation. From r9.0.0 an answer over 90 days is read back in months and days and confirmed before moving on (D-53); nothing up to 3650 is refused.

stem.text: Does your family manage or control your social media use?
How does your family manage or control your social media use?

items.researcherNote: Asked only if sm_family_control = Yes (D-53). Study-defined options, not a published measure; 8 = something else, described in sm_family_control_other.

options.label: They set time limits or times when I can't use it
They use parental controls or a monitoring app
They decide which apps or sites I can use
They check my messages, posts or who I follow
They know my passwords or can get into my accounts
They take my phone or device away at certain times
They have to agree before I get a new app or account

stem.text: What else does your family do?

items.researcherNote: Free text, asked only when 'Something else' is chosen in sm_family_control_how (D-53).

blocks.name: YBM screen control and social-media impact

stem.text: I can control my screen behaviours
I feel dependent on screens in order to function effectively in day-to-day life
I feel addicted to any screen based activities
The impacts of social media on my mental wellbeing are mostly positive

items.researcherNote: D-07: administered stem read 'my mental welling is mostly positive'. Legacy row code 4.

stem.text: The impacts of social media on my wellbeing are mostly negative

items.researcherNote: D-07: administered stem read 'my wellbeing in mostly negative'. Legacy row code 5.

stem.text: Social media is essential for day-to-day life
I avoid some social media
At what times of day do you usually use social media?

items.researcherNote: Study-written (D-67). One variable per time of day.

options.label: During the school or work day
When I wake up in the night

stem.text: When do you use social media the most?

items.researcherNote: Study-written (D-67). Same codes as smp_times_of_day.

options.label: During the school or work day
When I wake up in the night

stem.text: Which best describes how you use social media during a day?

items.researcherNote: Study-written (D-67). Long sessions vs frequent short checks.

options.label: Lots of short checks spread through the day
It changes a lot from day to day

stem.text: On a typical day, about how many times do you think you pick up or glance at your phone, even without unlocking it?

items.researcherNote: Study-written (D-67). Perceived checking. Compare with phone_pickups (ybm_phone_pickups) where that module is asked.

stem.text: I scroll past videos or posts without watching or reading them all the way through.
I skip ahead or speed up videos instead of watching them normally.
When I'm on social media, I'm really paying attention to what I'm watching or reading.
I do other things while I scroll, like homework, TV or talking to people.
I realise I've been scrolling without really taking anything in.
I open a social media app without really meaning to.
Please look at your phone's Screen Time or Digital Wellbeing. Can you see how many times you picked up or unlocked your phone yesterday?

lede.text: On an iPhone: Settings → Screen Time → See All App & Website Activity → Pickups. On Android: Settings → Digital Wellbeing → Unlocks.

items.researcherNote: Study-written (D-67). The number is asked only for 1 = Yes.

options.label: I don't have my phone with me

stem.text: What number does it show for yesterday?

items.researcherNote: Device-recorded pickups (iPhone) or unlocks (Android) yesterday, as read by the participant (D-67).

blocks.citation: Possibly derived from Sharma, B., Lee, S. S., & Johnson, B. K. (2022), Technology, Mind, and Behavior — source verification outstanding (A-23).

I feel pretty worried or upset when I think or know somebody is angry at me

When I see an opportunity for something I like I get excited right away
